picks.headline: Tautomer-Predictor AI Tool Identifies Stable Molecules for Drug Discovery
picks.excerpt: NYU's open-source graph neural network, trained on 1.1M tautomeric states, predicts hydrogen positions for 4.6M compounds in hours and flags 126 misassigned ligands in the Protein Data Bank (Chemical Science).
picks.rationale: The freshest item in the pool (09-23). It is an open-source GNN with hard numbers (4.6M compounds in hours) and a concrete finding: 126 misassigned PDB ligands. Covers chemistry.

picks.headline: Virtual cells built from 4D AI models and 'digital twins' could speed up drug discovery
picks.excerpt: UC San Diego (Cell) trained the MitoSpace deep-learning model on 40,000 drug-treated 4D lattice light-sheet cell movies to predict cellular health from mitochondrial shape (75% vs 56% for 2D), plus physics-based digital-twin cells that predict drug-induced changes.
picks.rationale: A Cell paper with a measurable gain from 4D over 2D (75% vs 56%), plus physics-based digital-twin cells. Covers cell biology. It is a different study from the 09-22 'AI tool cell million years' story.

picks.headline: AI tool nears psychiatrist-level accuracy
picks.excerpt: UTHealth Houston and Yale built a Qwen3-Omni-based system that analyzes patient video (speech, tone, behavior) to perform mental status exams with accuracy comparable to psychiatric teams (npj Mental Health Research).
picks.rationale: Multimodal AI on patient video performs mental status exams about as accurately as psychiatric teams. Covers psychiatry and psychology. It is a clinical study, not the opinion pieces in the pool.

picks.headline: Scientists develop real-time AI monitoring for an advanced nuclear reactor component
picks.excerpt: Argonne National Laboratory pairs explainable-AI algorithms with distributed fiber-optic sensors to detect coolant blockages in molten-salt reactor heat exchangers in real time (Scientific Reports).
picks.rationale: Argonne pairs explainable AI with fiber-optic sensing to monitor molten-salt reactors in real time. Covers physics and nuclear engineering, which the section has not covered recently. It was held as backfill on 09-23 and is not yet published.

picks.headline: What is your dog really saying? AI is helping researchers decode animal communication
picks.excerpt: Kaunas University of Technology researchers use machine learning to break animal vocalizations into frequency/time features and infer emotional states; models like Dog2vec, trained on 6,000+ hours of barks, find patterns the human ear misses.
picks.rationale: Machine learning decodes emotional states from animal vocalizations; Dog2vec was trained on 6,000+ hours of barks. Covers animal behavior, and it is fresh (09-22). Chosen over the right-whale study (09-16) for recency, which also keeps Phys.org at 2 picks.
